emma_support: FYI customer report - dedicated pool pinned to eu-west-1 but ~30% of requests are going to hosted eu-west-2 and they see 250-400ms extra latency. ticket #INC-12345 :thinking_face:
ryan_infra: Oof. Any repro or sample request ids?
miguel_oncall: Paging routing team — seeing cross-region bounce in traces?
emma_support: Yes, customer gave these request ids: `req_8a7f2`, `req_8a7f3`. They repro with our SDK against region=eu-west-1.
dani_router: Can you paste the routing decision logs for one id? I want to see why affinity pin didn't match.
emma_support: Pasting a trimmed log for `req_8a7f2`:
```
2026-03-16T14:12:01Z request=req_8a7f2 tenant=acme-corp route_key=eu-west-1 pinned_pool=dedicated-eu-1 pin_ttl=3600
2026-03-16T14:12:01Z routing: pool_lookup -> dedicated-eu-1 (healthy=false)
2026-03-16T14:12:01Z routing: fallback -> hosted-eu-2 selected by cost-heuristic
2026-03-16T14:12:01Z proxy: upstream=hosted-eu-2 latency_ms=18
```
ryan_infra: Interesting - `healthy=false` on the dedicated pool. Any recent evictions or autoscale events?
miguel_oncall: I see an autoscaler churn earlier that marked 3 nodes as draining around `14:10Z`. Might be transient.
emma_support: Customer says this started after a maintenance window last night.
dani_router: Two things to confirm: 1) is tenant pin stored in tenant metadata (not ephemeral) 2) does routing policy respect pins even if pool signals unready?
ryan_infra: Current policy: prefer pinned dedicated pool, but if pool health==unready for >5s we route to fallback. There was a recent change to tighten SLOs so we lowered the unready threshold from 10s to 2s (PR #4123).
emma_support: That sounds like the cause - customers with short maintenance blips get spilled to hosted and see higher latency/billing differences. Customer is on committed dedicated contract, so this is a billing + SLA problem.
billing_ops: Can confirm customer got billed at hosted rates for these spilled requests. Need to reconcile. I'll open a billing adjustment if we confirm root cause.
dani_router: Repro steps from my side: run `curl -H "x-region: eu-west-1" -H "x-tenant: acme-corp" https://api.redwood.ai/generate` in a loop while toggling node health flag. I can simulate node drain via `kubectl cordon` in staging to reproduce evict->fallback.
ryan_infra: Please add exact commands you ran.
dani_router: Steps:
```
# 1. create tenant pin
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"tenant":"acme-corp","pin":"dedicated-eu-1","ttl":3600}' https://admin.local/pins
# 2. send requests
for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -H "x-tenant: acme-corp" -H "x-region: eu-west-1" https://staging.api.local/generate >/dev/null & done
# 3. cordon a node
kubectl cordon node-9 -n redwood-serving
# 4. watch routing logs
kubectl logs -l app=router -n redwood-serving | grep acme-corp
```
miguel_oncall: I ran that in staging — behaviour matches production: after `cordon` we mark pool.unready -> requests flow to hosted in ~3s.
emma_support: Customer impact: higher latency, hosted billing, and some 503s when hosted saturates. They've escalated to legal for SLA credits.
ryan_infra: Short term mitigation: revert the unready threshold change (PR #4123) to previous 10s, so brief maintenance doesn't cause immediate spillover.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: revert-pr-4123 -> infra-router-config at 2026-03-16T15:05:00Z by ryan_infra
ryan_infra: I'll tag for emergency rollback and schedule a canary in eu-west-1 for 10m.
dani_router: Also recommend we change the fallback policy for pinned tenants: if tenant has active pin, prefer queueing requests to pinned pool (up to X pending) rather than immediate fallback. That avoids billing surprises. Filing design doc.
emma_support: Customer wants an immediate credit and confirmation when fixed.
billing_ops: I'll provisionally credit the last 12 hours for this tenant and hold further billing until we confirm resolution. Need ticket with affected request ids (emma, please attach).
emma_support: Attached logs + request ids in INC-12345.
miguel_oncall: Rollback completed and canary running. Early metrics: spillover rate dropped from 28% -> 2% over 7 minutes.
monitor-bot: Alert resolved: routed-spillover-high (eu-west-1) -> cleared at 2026-03-16T15:12:30Z
ryan_infra: Next steps: 1) revert is live, 2) design change for queued pref for pinned tenants, 3) add a metric for `pin-induced-spillover` and a billing safeguard to prevent hosted billing for pinned tenants during short maintenance (if possible), 4) postmortem.
dani_router: I'll draft the design and include config examples. Sample policy idea:
```
fallback_policy:
  pinned_behavior: queue-with-timeout
  queue_timeout_ms: 500
  max_queue_depth: 50
```
emma_support: Customer updated: "Thanks for the fast response — we saw requests stabilise and appreciate the credit." :white_check_mark:
ryan_infra: I'll own the postmortem and timeline. Assigning to myself.
emma_support: Thanks all. Closing for now but will follow up on design doc and billing closure.
miguel_oncall: marking incident resolved and adding follow-up: increase canary coverage next maintenance.
